llm.summary: The skill's purpose (sending/receiving emails for agents) is plausible, but the instructions ask you to create and store secrets, rely on third-party services, and reference install/deploy artifacts that are not included or declared — these mismatches warrant caution.

dimensions.detail: The claimed capability (send/receive/search emails and extract verification codes) matches the runtime instructions. However the SKILL.md asserts 'Full control, no third-party dependency' while the instructions require Cloudflare Workers and a Resend account/API key—contradictory claims. Also the registry metadata declares no required credentials, but the onboarding clearly expects secrets (RESEND_API_KEY, AUTH_TOKEN, Cloudflare access).
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Instructions tell the user/agent to globally install an npm package, deploy a Cloudflare Worker, create a D1 database, set wrangler secrets, and store worker_url/worker_token in ~/.mails/config.json. Those steps are consistent with building an email service, but they direct creation and storage of auth secrets and long-polling for verification codes (which will be printed to stdout). The instructions do not instruct reading unrelated system files, though SDK examples show attaching local files (expected for sending attachments).
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill is instruction-only (no bundled code), yet the onboarding expects a 'worker' directory and an npm package 'mails-agent' to be installed. The registry entry provides no source URL or homepage to inspect. Installing an unvetted global npm package and deploying worker code from an unspecified source increases risk because you cannot review the code that will run on your machine or in your Cloudflare account.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Registry metadata lists no required env vars/credentials, but the SKILL.md requires a Resend API key, a Cloudflare Worker AUTH_TOKEN, and Cloudflare account access to enable Email Routing and create D1. Those credentials are necessary for the described functionality, but the mismatch between declared requirements and actual instructions is a red flag. The skill asks the user to persist secrets locally (~/.mails/config.json) and in Worker secrets.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request 'always: true' and is user-invocable. It stores its own configuration in ~/.mails/config.json and the Worker uses its own secrets. Autonomous invocation is allowed by default; combined with the ability to send emails and capture verification codes this gives the agent capabilities that could be abused if the skill or its underlying code are malicious — not inherently wrong, but worth reviewing before granting.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill could do what it claims, but there are several mismatches and missing pieces you should address before installing: 1) The README asks you to use Cloudflare and Resend and to store secrets (RESEND_API_KEY, AUTH_TOKEN), yet the registry lists no required credentials—assume you must provide and protect those keys. 2) There is no homepage or source code included in the package metadata and the skill bundle contains no worker code; do NOT blindly npm install a global package you cannot inspect. 3) Verify the 'mails-agent' npm package and the Worker code: check the publisher, review source code, and prefer installing from a known repository or building the Worker yourself. 4) Use least-privilege keys (dedicated Resend key, separate Cloudflare account if possible), rotate/revoke keys after testing, and host the Worker under a domain/account you control. 5) If you cannot review the code or confirm the package source, treat this skill as risky and consider alternatives (self-hosted solutions you audit or reputable providers).
